summary: Replaced the multi-task /orchestrate classifier's unconditional blocked verdict with a six-branch discriminating arm across 8 plan phases: empty dependencies[] / dependency abandoned-or-expanded / dependency outstanding / handoff blockers present / previous_status missing or unrecognized / discharged. A discharged blocked candidate (all dependencies[] status exactly "completed", no handoff blockers) now routes via previous_status through the classifier's existing status-routing logic for BOTH engines, converging mt and single; every non-discharged sub-case preserves today's skip(mt)/needs_human(single) divergence with a specific named reason. Propagated the change through the classifier's own header table/justification/schema docs, its test suite (12 new fixtures, all confirmed RED pre-fix), the dry-run report's reason threading, both orchestrate skills' blocked handlers and grouping tables, the state-machine doc's state row, and the guardrails Gate Catalogue (3 new rows). Deployed and verified from .claude/scripts/; only two pre-existing, unrelated verify-deploy.sh findings remain (confirmed via git log to predate this task).

artifacts.summary: Cause re-derivation, discriminator design, prior-Decision-3 narrowing, and full co-maintenance edit set with file/line anchors.

8-phase plan (4 waves) for the discriminating blocked classifier row: state.json dependency lookup discriminator, atomic-batch mechanism phase, fixture guard against candidate-list-membership implementations, Gate Catalogue and dry-run threading.

Discriminating blocked classifier arm shipped across 8 phases: classifier mechanism, its fixtures, dry-run reason threading, both orchestrate skills, the state-machine doc, and the guardrails Gate Catalogue all converged on the narrowed premise.

decisions_made: Dependency status is resolved via a second select(.project_number == $d) against the already-slurped $all array, bound through '. as $d' (a jq dot-context pitfall discovered and fixed during Phase 2), never via candidate-list ($candidates) membership -- verified by a fixture whose dependency is deliberately absent from the classifier's own argument list.
Empty dependencies[] is its own FIRST branch, evaluated before the all-completed check, so a vacuous 'all' over an empty list never discharges.
Discharge requires literal "completed", never the broader is_terminal set; a dependency stuck at abandoned/expanded gets its own loud needs_human branch.

A discharged candidate with a missing or unrecognized previous_status never guesses -- stays needs_human with a named reason (this is a distinct sixth branch beyond the plan's five-sub-case estimate, added because Testing & Validation explicitly requires it).

No status-rewrite component was added: the stale blocked string is overwritten by the dispatched skill's own skill_preflight_update, the same mechanism the shipped researching/planning convergence already relies on.

single engine's DISCHARGED blocked case now also routes through previous_status (converging with mt), applying the classifier header's own audit discriminator honestly -- both engines independently implement the non-discharged divergence in their own handlers, but neither independently implements a discharged-case divergence, so it converges.
Two out-of-plan-file-list repairs made and recorded as deviations: Stage 6's opening sentence (Phase 4) and index-entries.json's line_count (Phase 8, file_scope widened via state-write.sh).
dead_ends: Discriminator based on 'is the dependency present in the classifier's own CLI candidate list' ($candidates membership) was rejected per the research report and reconfirmed empirically: this is exactly the reproduction scenario, since a just-completed predecessor drops out of eligible_tasks before the successor is reclassified.
